redOnBase.decisiveLine: RED ON BASE 8672a5f00: xAI login row does not offer Grok subscription sign-in

decision: Follow OpenCode for the wire, as the owner directed. The shared public client is permitted; Mercury sends its own User-Agent and referrer, never another product's identity.

facts.fact: All three clients share public client b1a00492-073a-47ea-816f-4c329264a828. OpenCode explicitly calls it public; OpenClaw explicitly calls it shared, warning that consent can say Grok Build.

RFC 8628 device flow, no callback or client secret: POST https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/device/code, then POST https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token with client_id, device_code and grant_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code. Browser authorize endpoint exists but is not this flow.

Form-encoded requests; scope openid profile email offline_access grok-cli:access api:access. Device reply carries device_code, user_code, verification_uri, optional verification_uri_complete, expires_in and interval. authorization_pending waits; slow_down increases delay at least five seconds; access_denied, authorization_denied and expired_token terminate.

Refresh uses the same token endpoint, form grant_type=refresh_token with refresh_token and client_id, no secret. Access expiry is expires_in when stated, otherwise JWT exp is an observed hint; no fixed token lifetime is guaranteed. OpenCode defaults missing expires_in to one hour but Mercury does not treat that as a provider fact.

OpenCode leaves its SDK base at https://api.x.ai/v1 and injects Authorization: Bearer <access token> and its own User-Agent. Default transport is Responses; the LLM package also offers chat. Mercury subscription turns use /responses on that base, its own User-Agent, flat tools and stateless replay. API keys retain their existing chat road.

Model access must be read using the selected credential; no verified account model inventory is available without sign-in. Mercury uses GET /v1/models on OpenCode's API base and never seeds a subscription-only model list from the other clients' defaults.

OpenClaw differs: OAuth Responses and /models ride https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1; inference adds X-XAI-Token-Auth: xai-grok-cli, x-grok-client-version and x-grok-model-override. These alternate-host headers are NOT sent by Mercury.

OpenClaw reads GET https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits with bearer, x-grok-client-mode=cli and x-grok-client-version=1.0.4. It reads subscription_tier, config.creditUsagePercent, currentPeriod.type/start/end, legacy used/monthlyLimit; explicit zero is a fact, omitted percent is not zero. Prepaid balance is separate; onDemand counters are not included subscription quota. No such read appears in the pinned OpenCode auth plugin; repository code searches for cli-chat-proxy.grok.com and creditUsagePercent returned zero matches. Per owner's ruling Mercury does NOT read this alternative pool endpoint.

No subscription-specific 429 body, numeric allowance, reset or plan claim is established for OpenCode's road in these sources. Mercury keeps ordinary HTTP 429 / Retry-After handling, reports the Grok pool as unread and invents no window, tier or credits.

xAI announces SuperGrok or X Premium sign-in for OpenClaw on every tier and describes headless device codes; Hermes warns of backend tier eligibility refusals despite successful browser login. A login is not proof that inference is admitted.
